title: The 100% Rectal Cancer Cure Without Surgery & Next-Gen Synthetic Lethality: dMMR/MSI-H (Dostarlimab), MTA-Cooperative PRMT5 & Werner (WRN) Helicase — Dostarlimab 100% cCR Rectal & Pan-Solid Organ Sparing, MTA-Cooperative PRMT5 & WRN Helicase (PDB 2O8B, 4P7A, 7WSL, 7S1S, 6YHR)

teenKit.tldr: A revolutionary cancer immunotherapy drug called Dostarlimab has achieved a 100% cure rate in specific rectal cancers without needing surgery, by exploiting a breakdown in the tumor's DNA repair system.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This breakthrough proves that certain cancers can be entirely eliminated using the body's own immune system, sparing patients from life-altering surgeries and radiation.
keyTakeaways: DNA mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR) causes tumors to accumulate massive errors, making them vulnerable targets for immunotherapy.
Dostarlimab is a checkpoint inhibitor that wakes up exhausted immune cells so they can hunt down and destroy cancer tissue.
Advanced molecular targeting like PRMT5 and WRN helicase inhibitors are expanding these non-surgical cures to other complex, resistant tumor types.

vocab.meaning: A cellular glitch where cells fail to fix typos in their DNA, creating a high volume of mutations that flags them for immune destruction.
An antibody drug that blocks PD-1 proteins, essentially removing the blindfold that prevents the immune system from attacking cancer cells.
A cancer-killing strategy where knocking out a second backup gene finishes off a tumor that already has one broken mutation.
When advanced medical imaging and biopsies show zero remaining traces of active cancer in a patient's body.

quiz.question: What primary mechanism makes dMMR/MSI-H tumors uniquely vulnerable to drugs like Dostarlimab?
options: They grow much slower than normal cells
They have broken DNA repair systems that produce thousands of mutation flags for the immune system
They are immune to all forms of radiation
quiz.explanation: Their chaotic, mutation-heavy nature makes them look deeply foreign and obvious to an awakened immune system.

quiz.question: What was the landmark clinical result achieved by Cercek and Diaz at Memorial Sloan Kettering for dMMR rectal cancer patients?
options: A 50% reduction in tumor size requiring minor surgery
A 100% complete clinical response allowing patients to avoid surgery entirely
A complete cure only when combined with high-dose chemotherapy
Temporary remission lasting less than six months
quiz.explanation: Every single patient in the trial achieved a complete clinical response, completely eliminating the need for pelvic surgery.

quiz.question: What is the role of PD-1 in the context of cancer evasion?
options: It acts as a shield protein that tricks immune cells into leaving the cancer alone
It speeds up the rate of tumor metastasis
It repairs damaged DNA inside cancer cells
It feeds glucose to the tumor
quiz.explanation: PD-1 acts as an off-switch for T-cells, which cancer cells exploit to hide from the immune system.
